title: Affine open refinement of a pointed finite-over-smooth diagram
statement: Let $W_1,V,S_1$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $n\geq0$, let $\pi_1:W_1\to V$ be finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and let $h_1:V\to S_1$ be smooth of relative dimension $n$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Assume that every fibre of $h_1$ remains integral after every extension of its residue field [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible, def-pc-integral-scheme]. Fix $w_1\in W_1$, $y_1=\pi_1(w_1)$ and $s_1=h_1(y_1)$ with $\pi_1^{-1}(\{y_1\})=\{w_1\}$. There exist affine open neighbourhoods $U\subseteq S_1$ of $s_1$ and $Y\subseteq h_1^{-1}(U)$ of $y_1$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-open-immersion] such that the restricted map $h:Y\to U$ is surjective (on underlying points) [def-weil-surjective-morphism], smooth of relative dimension $n$, and has geometrically integral fibres, including nonemptiness after every residue-field extension. The inverse image $W=W_1\times_VY=\pi_1^{-1}(Y)$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is affine and open in $W_1$, and its projection $\pi:W\to Y$ is finite with $\pi^{-1}(\{y_1\})=\{w_1\}$. Under the open immersions $W\hookrightarrow W_1$, $Y\hookrightarrow V$ and $U\hookrightarrow S_1$, the marked points and all three residue fields [def-weil-residue-field] are unchanged, compatibly with the residue field maps induced by $\pi_1$ and $h_1$. The restricted square commutes: $h_1|_Y=i_Uh$ and $\pi_1|_W=i_Y\pi$, where $i_U:U\hookrightarrow S_1$ and $i_Y:Y\hookrightarrow V$ are the inclusions.

source.place: Tag 057L, lemma-local-local-structure-finite-type-affine, proof: U prime, V prime, image W prime, U double prime, and the finite inverse image.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] first in $S_1$ to choose an affine open $U_0$ containing $s_1$, and then in $V$ to the open $h_1^{-1}(U_0)$ containing $y_1$, to choose an affine open $Y_0$ with $y_1\in Y_0\subseteq h_1^{-1}(U_0)$.

source.place: Tag 057L, lemma-local-local-structure-finite-type-affine, choices U prime and V prime; Schemes Tag 01IT, lemma-basis-affine-opens

proof.text: By [lem-pc-smooth-flat], $h_1$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open] makes $h_1$ an open map. Thus $O=h_1(Y_0)$ is open in $S_1$, contains $s_1$ and lies in $U_0$. Choose an affine open $U$ with $s_1\in U\subseteq O$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis].

source.place: Tag 057L, lemma-local-local-structure-finite-type-affine, image W prime and choice U double prime; Morphisms Tags 01VF, 01VE and 01UA, lemma-smooth-flat, lemma-smooth-locally-finite-presentation and lemma-fppf-open (together Tag 056G, lemma-smooth-open)

proof.text: Factor $h_1|_{Y_0}$ through $U_0$ using [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]. Set $Y=Y_0\cap h_1^{-1}(U)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product], $Y=Y_0\times_{U_0}U$, compatibly with the inclusions and restricted maps. All three schemes $Y_0,U_0,U$ are affine, so [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] makes $Y$ affine. It is open in $V$, contains $y_1$, and lies in $h_1^{-1}(U)$. The same factorization lemma gives $h:Y\to U$ with $i_Uh=h_1|_Y$.

source.place: Tag 057L, lemma-local-local-structure-finite-type-affine, equality with U double prime times V prime over U prime; Schemes Tags 01HI, 01JR, 01I4 and 01JQ, lemma-restrict-map-to-opens, lemma-open-fibre-product, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes and lemma-fibre-product-affines

proof.text: For each $s\in U\subseteq h_1(Y_0)$ there is $y\in Y_0$ with $h_1(y)=s$. This $y$ lies in $Y_0\cap h_1^{-1}(U)=Y$, and $h(y)=s$. Thus $h$ is surjective by [def-weil-surjective-morphism].

source.place: Tag 057L, lemma-local-local-structure-finite-type-affine, surjectivity of the restricted morphism

proof.text: The property smooth of relative dimension n [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] is Zariski local at source and target in Mathlib (via HasRingHomProperty for Locally (IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension n)). Therefore IsZariskiLocalAtSource.resLE applied to h_1 gives SmoothOfRelativeDimension n h directly, as the relative-dimension version of [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes]. No comparison of topological dimensions is needed.

source.place: Tag 01V6, lemma-smooth-characterize, restriction to opens; Tag 02G2, definition-smooth-relative-dimension; Schemes Tag 01JR, lemma-open-fibre-product

proof.text: Fix a field K and a morphism x : Spec K → U [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Surjectivity of h is preserved by base change [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change], so Y ×_U Spec K is nonempty. The commuting restriction square gives a map Y ×_U Spec K → V ×_{S_1} Spec K, with the ambient field-valued map x followed by U → S_1. It is an open immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product]. For an arbitrary chosen pullback square, the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] supplies its isomorphism to this canonical pullback. This avoids any iterated-fibre or residue-field identification in the integrality argument.

source.place: Tag 057L, lemma-local-local-structure-finite-type-affine, nonempty open subschemes of geometric fibres; Morphisms Tag 01S1, lemma-base-change-surjective; Schemes Tag 01JR, lemma-open-fibre-product

proof.text: The hypothesis GeometricallyIntegral h_1 makes V ×_{S_1} Spec K integral for every field-valued map to S_1 [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible, def-pc-integral-scheme]. A nonempty open subscheme of an integral scheme is integral: its nonempty opens are nonempty opens of the ambient scheme with the same section rings. Apply Mathlib isIntegral_of_isOpenImmersion to the composite of the pullback comparison isomorphism and the open immersion from Step 6. This proves the universal field-valued pullback condition defining GeometricallyIntegral h.

source.place: Tag 057L, lemma-local-local-structure-finite-type-affine, final fibre assertion; Properties Tag 01OK, definition-integral

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product], $W=W_1\times_VY$ is the open subscheme $\pi_1^{-1}(Y)$ of $W_1$, with projection $\pi:W\to Y$ and $i_Y\pi=\pi_1|_W$. Apply (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence] to the finite $\pi_1$ and $Y\to V$: $\pi$ is finite. By (b) of that node, $W$ is affine because $Y$ is affine. The marked $w_1$ lies in $W$ since $\pi_1(w_1)=y_1\in Y$. Set-theoretically, $\pi^{-1}(\{y_1\})=\pi_1^{-1}(\{y_1\})\cap W=\{w_1\}$.

source.place: Tag 057L, lemma-local-local-structure-finite-type-affine, opening sentence and finite inverse image; Morphisms Tags 01WL and 01S8, lemma-base-change-finite and lemma-characterize-affine

proof.text: For each of $W\hookrightarrow W_1$, $Y\hookrightarrow V$ and $U\hookrightarrow S_1$, [def-weil-open-immersion] identifies the structure sheaf with the restriction of the ambient one. Neighbourhoods contained in the open are cofinal among all neighbourhoods of the marked point, so the stalk, its maximal ideal and its quotient residue field [def-weil-residue-field] are canonically unchanged. The commutative restriction identities $i_Uh=h_1|_Y$ and $i_Y\pi=\pi_1|_W$ identify the maps on these stalks: both send a germ to the germ of its pullback under the original map. Quotienting the identical local maps gives the same residue field maps. Thus all three marked points, residue fields and their maps have the claimed compatibility. In Lean the inclusion maps on points are Scheme.Opens.ι_apply, their residue maps are isomorphisms by the open-immersion instance, and the commuting squares give the displayed identities by Scheme.Hom.residueFieldMap_congr and Scheme.residueFieldMap_comp.

Step 5: smooth-restrict (a), open-fibre-product and the Lean-closed generic dimension-at-point-open-subspace give relative dimension n; def-kun-dimension is the topological min over opens, so the tool applies. Step 6: surjective-base-change gives nonempty fibres after every field extension K/κ(s). Step 7 (elementary): a nonempty open of an integral scheme is integral, which gives geometric integrality. Step 8: open-preimage-fibre-product and finite-permanence (a) and (b) make W = π_1^{-1}(Y) affine with π finite, and the singleton fibre is kept. Step 9 (elementary): stalks, residue fields and the induced maps are unchanged under the open immersions. All 17 Stacks tags match their labels in tags/tags. The statement is true: on S = Spec k, V = A^n, Y is a basic open and its fibres are geometrically integral. It also matches what the parent's step 3 uses. No duplicates in the DAG: the trf siblings cover the 057K étale-base and normal-morphism steps, not this refinement. Accepted tool_use: lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace in Step 5. One ordering remark only: κ_U(s) = κ_{S_1}(s) is used in Step 5 but written out in Steps 6 and 9; the content is present, so this is not a fault. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem exists_marked_finite_smooth_affine_refinement {W₁ V S₁ : Scheme.{u}} (n : ℕ) (π₁ : W₁ ⟶ V) (h₁ : V ⟶ S₁) [IsFinite π₁] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension n h₁] [GeometricallyIntegral h₁] (w₁ : W₁) (hπ : π₁ ⁻¹' ({π₁ w₁} : Set V) = ({w₁} : Set W₁)) : ∃ (U : S₁.Opens) (Y : V.Opens) (e : Y ≤ h₁ ⁻¹ᵁ U) (hy : π₁ w₁ ∈ Y), IsAffineOpen U ∧ IsAffineOpen Y ∧ Surjective (h₁.resLE U Y e) ∧ SmoothOfRelativeDimension n (h₁.resLE U Y e) ∧ GeometricallyIntegral (h₁.resLE U Y e) ∧ IsAffine (π₁ ⁻¹ᵁ Y).toScheme ∧ IsFinite (π₁ ∣_ Y) ∧ (π₁ ∣_ Y) ⁻¹' ({⟨π₁ w₁, hy⟩} : Set Y) = ({⟨w₁, hy⟩} : Set (π₁ ⁻¹ᵁ Y)) ∧ (π₁ ∣_ Y) ⟨w₁, hy⟩ = ⟨π₁ w₁, hy⟩ ∧ h₁.resLE U Y e ⟨π₁ w₁, hy⟩ = ⟨h₁ (π₁ w₁), e hy⟩ ∧ IsIso ((π₁ ⁻¹ᵁ Y).ι.residueFieldMap ⟨w₁, hy⟩) ∧ IsIso (Y.ι.residueFieldMap ⟨π₁ w₁, hy⟩) ∧ IsIso (U.ι.residueFieldMap ⟨h₁ (π₁ w₁), e hy⟩) ∧ h₁.resLE U Y e ≫ U.ι = Y.ι ≫ h₁ ∧ (π₁ ∣_ Y) ≫ Y.ι = (π₁ ⁻¹ᵁ Y).ι ≫ π₁ ∧ (V.residueFieldCongr (morphismRestrict_base_coe π₁ Y ⟨w₁, hy⟩)).hom ≫ π₁.residueFieldMap w₁ ≫ (π₁ ⁻¹ᵁ Y).ι.residueFieldMap ⟨w₁, hy⟩ = Y.ι.residueFieldMap ((π₁ ∣_ Y) ⟨w₁, hy⟩) ≫ (π₁ ∣_ Y).residueFieldMap ⟨w₁, hy⟩ ∧ (S₁.residueFieldCongr (h₁.coe_resLE_apply e ⟨π₁ w₁, hy⟩)).hom ≫ h₁.residueFieldMap (π₁ w₁) ≫ Y.ι.residueFieldMap ⟨π₁ w₁, hy⟩ = U.ι.residueFieldMap (h₁.resLE U Y e ⟨π₁ w₁, hy⟩) ≫ (h₁.resLE U Y e).residueFieldMap ⟨π₁ w₁, hy⟩
